speaker: AIDEN
text: The man taking tickets didn’t look up.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I’m Aiden. He looked at me. Looked at the six-foot photograph beside the door. Looked back.

speaker: TICKET
text: You look better in the picture.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Vegas. After the homecoming. I had been back long enough for these niggas to start charging admission to my problems. Somebody had put angel wings on a photograph of me getting arrested. Cropped out the cuffs, left the officer’s hand on my shoulder. Nigga had a police escort into heaven. I called Tank.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Why there a cover charge at my funeral?

speaker: AIDEN
text: I heard chewing. Nigga, are you eating?

speaker: AIDEN
text: I paid the forty. The nigga stamped DECEASED on my wrist.

speaker: TICKET
text: That gets you one well drink.

speaker: AIDEN
text: One? Nigga, the sign says two-drink minimum.

speaker: AIDEN
text: A nigga behind me shook his head.

speaker: GUEST
text: Hold up. Ain’t that the deceased?

speaker: AIDEN
text: Ticket man looked at my stamp.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The nigga pulled out his phone.

speaker: GUEST
text: People gonna think I knew you personally.

speaker: GUEST
text: Yeah, but the funeral picture hit different.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Shawna found me beside the chocolate fountain, turning my memorial program upside down.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Why this say I’m survived by eleven children?

speaker: AIDEN
text: My wife looked beautiful in black. Slit up one leg, diamond at her throat, hat tilted like she had already forgiven herself. You enjoying widowhood?

speaker: AIDEN
text: I pulled her close. She put two fingers against my mouth.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: Eight minutes. Kitchen. Stay there until we get the case.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, I could take it right now.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: And Silas’s men could start shooting into everybody who paid to eat shrimp.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I straightened up. Mercedes stood beside the stage in a red suit, thumb pressed into her palm. She’d been doing that all week. Silas Gold had stolen the original recordings of her first album. The nigga had locked the drive in a silver case and invited buyers to bid. She could sing every song again. She couldn’t rebuild the demolished studio, recall every musician to the same night, or make her voice crack exactly where it had in the last chorus. She had left that crack in. Said it sounded like her.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Silas lived behind bulletproof glass and sent other niggas out to be unpleasant. Tell him Aiden was dead, though, and suddenly the motherfucker wanted fresh air. Shawna had promised a private auction after the memorial. My watch, my cars, the collection. Silas would bring the recordings so they could settle everything together. Mercedes would inspect the case backstage. Porsche would switch it. I would stay in the fucking kitchen.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Mercedes caught me looking and came to fix my collar.

speaker: MERCEDES
text: The thing where this becomes about you.

speaker: AIDEN
text: My photograph is six feet tall.

speaker: MERCEDES
text: Exactly. The nigga has enough publicity.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I stopped smiling. You’ll get your music.

speaker: MERCEDES
text: I know. I want to enjoy getting it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She squeezed my shoulder and went back to the stage. Shawna kissed me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, y’all got one word for me tonight. She turned me toward the door.

speaker: AIDEN
text: They had hired a full band. Horns, two keyboards, drummer wearing sunglasses he hadn’t removed for either prayer.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank took the microphone carrying a plate.

speaker: TANK
text: We gathered here because my brother would want these niggas supporting the bar.

speaker: TANK
text: Aiden was generous. Nigga gave me the shirt off his back.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I leaned toward the kitchen speaker.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Police was looking for a man in a red shirt.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I pushed through the kitchen door. Shawna held up one finger without turning around.

speaker: TANK
text: Came to the station. Told them I hadn’t done shit. Paid everything. Waited six hours. Bought me breakfast.

speaker: AIDEN
text: My palm rested against the door.

speaker: TANK
text: Then the nigga asked for his shirt.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The drummer caught the laugh with a roll. I had to smile. Nigga knew when to hit.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Silas Gold entered in a white fur coat. Four men followed him. Smallest nigga carried the silver case. Biggest had a neck wider than my thigh and an expression like somebody assembled him without the last page.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank looked at the closed coffin.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Silas laughed. His niggas joined a second late.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Shawna offered her hand. He bent to kiss it. She moved it just enough that his mouth met his own thumb.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: Mercedes inspects them first. We agreed.

speaker: SILAS
text: Darling, look at the crowd. Can’t buy timing.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He took the microphone from Tank and balanced his bottle on my coffin.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The drummer gave them a little tick, tick, tick.

speaker: AIDEN
text: From the kitchen I mouthed, Nigga, you stole my boat.

speaker: SILAS
text: But he was a man of appetite.

speaker: SILAS
text: Appetite leaves things unfinished. People unprovided for. I would never presume—

speaker: AIDEN
text: Silas waited out the laughter with his teeth showing.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The case opened. Silas put his bottle on the coffin and took out the hard drive.

speaker: SILAS
text: Perhaps our little lady could sing a tribute. And apologize for some things she’s said about me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The biggest nigga blocked the backstage doorway. Porsche stood behind him with the duplicate case.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Silas offered Mercedes the microphone. Pulled it back.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The cook looked up from his potatoes.

speaker: COOK
text: Nigga, you want me to hold that?

speaker: AIDEN
text: I looked through the round window.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Shawna saw my hands, looked at the stage, and shifted her chair clear of the aisle.

speaker: AIDEN
text: A woman near the aisle looked from me to the coffin.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The nigga beside her crossed himself.

speaker: AIDEN
text: They moved. I passed between them without losing a shrimp.

speaker: AIDEN
text: From the stage, the drummer lifted one stick and watched me approach.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I stopped beside the smallest nigga.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Silas heard me. Turned so fast the fur collar slapped his mouth.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He shoved the microphone into its stand and reached inside his coat.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I drove the tray under his wrist. The pistol fired through the ceiling, flew from his hand, and skidded under the piano. Plaster burst over the stage. The trumpet player ducked. Tank tackled two guests behind a table without spilling his drink.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I caught Silas by the coat.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He grabbed his bottle from the coffin and swung. Glass broke against my shoulder. Pain ran down my arm.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I hit him with the tray.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The drive flew from his other hand. Mercedes caught it against her chest.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The biggest nigga lunged. Porsche hooked his ankle with the duplicate case. He stumbled down the steps into the chair Shawna had picked up.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He sat carefully among the pieces.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Mercedes tucked the drive inside her jacket. Behind me, another man drew a gun. I saw him in the mirrored wall and ducked as she threw the microphone stand over my head with both hands.

speaker: AIDEN
text: It hit the nigga across the chest and carried him into the drum kit.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The drummer stood. Looked at his broken cymbal. Looked at the man under it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Then he hit him with the stool.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Silas wriggled free of his coat. Ran for the steps. Tank caught him around the waist, flung open the coffin with his free hand, and tipped him inside.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The coffin rocked. Lid banged shut.

speaker: AIDEN
text: A little man in a gold tracksuit sat upright underneath Silas, wearing my spare sunglasses and looking ready to fight the entire funeral.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The little man pointed at Tank.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank pointed at the dust hanging over the stage.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The little man climbed over Silas’s stomach and straightened his tracksuit.

speaker: CORPSE_PERFORMER
text: I do the surprise. I do the dance. I leave. Ain’t no nigga mentioned wrestling.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Silas’s fourth man backed toward the exit. Tank pointed at him without looking away from me.

speaker: TANK
text: Sit your ass down. The nigga hasn’t danced.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The smallest man still held the empty case and a shrimp tail. He lowered the case very slowly.

speaker: COOK
text: No the fuck you are not.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Seven minutes to collect the guns, tie up Silas’s men, and convince everybody the bar remained open.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Silas kept trying to sit up in the coffin. The little man eased him down with a sneaker against his forehead.

speaker: CORPSE_PERFORMER
text: Stop being in my office, nigga.

speaker: AIDEN
text: At the sound desk, Mercedes took the drive from her jacket and plugged it in. Files appeared. She chose one, listened through the headphones, and closed her eyes.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Porsche took her hand beneath the table.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I moved closer. Shawna caught my belt and pulled me back.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Mercedes removed the headphones and wiped under one eye.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She looked around. Overturned flowers. Two men bleeding into memorial napkins. My giant face leaning crookedly against the wall.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Then she went to the stage.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The drummer was fitting a spare cymbal.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She gave the sound man a track number. A hiss came through the speakers, then saxophone, warm and rough. The band found its rhythm.

speaker: MERCEDES
text: Turn that nigga around. I need the room.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She sang low at first, almost speaking. Bass came underneath. She planted a heel against the monitor and let the next line climb. By the chorus, people stood between fallen chairs finding somebody to dance with.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The little man shut the coffin and started dancing on it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Porsche laughed with her face turned up. The cook came out with my jacket over his shoulder and a tray in his hands. A woman took the tray, put it on a table, and pulled him onto the floor.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Shawna slipped her fingers into mine.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She touched my sleeve. I winced.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She stayed against my good side.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The last chorus came. Mercedes’s younger voice caught for half a breath through the speakers. Onstage, she sang alongside it, smiling. Porsche stopped laughing to listen.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: Eleven sponsors is a lot of mouths to feed.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I laughed and hurt my shoulder again.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The ticket man opened the door for another group.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He nodded toward Mercedes, the man dancing on the coffin, and me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: By the time the police took Silas away, the band had demanded overtime and Tank was negotiating for the leftover shrimp.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The young sound technician came over with two clean glasses. Twenty-three, little beard, still looking between Shawna and my DECEASED wrist stamp.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, apparently you can charge for it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: My wife laughed before I opened my mouth.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: So was I. One of us remembers who saved whom.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The technician pulled up a chair.

speaker: TANK
text: Somebody get this nigga a plate,

speaker: TANK
text: So am I. I organized a death.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Mercedes passed the young man a napkin. Porsche moved the bottle closer. He loosened the headphones around his neck and sat.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank dragged over another chair. Shawna sat against my good side and took one of the glasses.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I looked at the nigga who had asked.

speaker: AIDEN
text: First night in Vegas. You want the whole thing?

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, we still waiting on that chapter.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I took a drink. Back then, before any of these niggas knew what we'd become, the bass was shaking a different wall. Big T had his hand on my shoulder, and twelve men waited beside the cars.
